'page' (the default), 'popup', 'side' (a side panel) or 'full' (full screen).
'popup' (the default), 'side' (a side panel) or 'page' (the Devices page).

12 or 24 hours; auto follows the browser’s language.
25d from a fixed angle above (angle, turn); 3d turned by camera.
25d shows the level raised, from a fixed angle above (turned by turn); 3d as a dollhouse to turn and zoom (Pro). Both need WebGL 2: low-power screens and Paper show 2D.
A 0–1 value as a percentage, written the region's way: 0.62 | percent → "62%" ("62 %" in Germany).

A 270° dial filled up to a value within a range (target temperature, battery, power); what you put inside it (the value in words) sits a little below the dial’s centre (move it with middle-y), or stands on the base line of a half circle. Part: ::part(middle).

A 270° dial you drag to set a numeric capability (target temperature): the knob is the value, an optional dot shows a second value (the room), and the value sits large in the middle. A value changed from elsewhere (the − and + buttons, the Homey, another screen) springs into place with one small overshoot; under your finger it follows exactly. Reduced motion and e-ink: it moves at once.
A May edit choice per dashboard or floor plan you share.

A PIN pad: dots, the keys 1–9, ⌫, 0 and ✓. The digits go to the server and nowhere else; the template never sees them. A right PIN (the account’s, set in Account) runs data-hd-on-unlock, whose event carries nothing; a wrong one shakes, and after 5 wrong in a row every keypad of the account waits 5 minutes. Works on a keyboard too (digits, Backspace, Enter, Escape). E.g. <hd-keypad label="Disarm" data-hd-on-unlock="set('homealarm_state', 'disarmed', settings.alarm.id)"></hd-keypad>.
A badge on its tab: a count (1 and up, 99+ past 99) or `dot`; empty or 0 shows none. Screen readers hear the count with the label.
A bar of dashboards to go between, on the grid or docked along an edge.

A battery whose charge fills it from the bottom: while it charges a wave rolls on the surface, while it gives power a shimmer runs down through it; low (under 20%) it turns warn. Reduced motion: still; e-ink snaps.
A bell swings and rings when the doorbell is pressed. The tile says Ringing while it does and Quiet after, with when it last rang underneath (“Rang 2 min ago”), or “No ring yet”.
A big lock that is one button: tap to lock, tap twice to unlock.
A blurred copy of the album art tints the whole card, strongest while it plays and fainter when paused. It looks lively next to calm tiles.
A button that opens a dashboard or a device, starts a flow, sets a mood or a variable.

A camera: its latest snapshot as the picture, live video over it while the tile is on screen (the host signals WebRTC with its own session, so the template never sees a token), a status pill (Live, Connecting…, Paused, Snapshot with its age, Unavailable) and, when asked, the camera’s name, a motion badge and an expand mark, over soft scrims. It streams only while visible, while the page is visible and the host allows it, never on e-ink (the snapshot only, refreshed), at most four at a time per page, and retries with backoff when a stream can’t start, showing the snapshot meanwhile. A video a browser can’t play (RTSP) isn’t tried: it shows the snapshot with a note saying so. It fills its parent and sets `data-state` on itself: connecting, live, paused, failed, snapshot or unavailable.
A camera’s picture, live while it is on screen. Tap to open it big.
A capability id of that device, quoted: 'onoff', 'evcharger_charging'.

A chart of any data, not only recorded readings: over time or categories as lines, areas, columns, stacked columns, steps, a scatter or a heatmap; or the shares of a whole as a pie, donut, rose, bar list, treemap, funnel or radar. The data comes from a data setting (source="{{ settings.source }}": a data feed, typed JSON, a text variable or Homey values, kept current) or as JSON in data (data="{{ list | json }}", at most 64 KB). Without paths it finds the numbers itself: a number list, [time, value] pairs, { "name": number } objects, or lists of objects. A list drawn as lines runs along its labels; lines drawn as a pie give each line’s latest value. Colours follow the theme’s chart colours; on e-ink the slices are named instead of coloured. What you put inside it (a donut’s total) is centred on the chart. Part: ::part(middle).
A cheap hour on price bars and in the energy widgets.
A check mark and “All quiet”.
A command is on its way to the Homey.
A command is on its way: present, or `true` (`false` is not busy), e.g. {% if pending.onoff %} busy{% endif %} or busy="{{ b.busy }}".

A condition Liquid can’t read itself is read as an expression, also in `elsif` and `unless`; every Liquid condition stays as it was. In an expression 0, empty text, null and false count as false (in Liquid only null and false do). Nothing is smaller or larger than null.
A dark map, whatever the theme.
A dashboard for every screen in the house: the desk, the wall, a phone and e-ink.
A data setting of the widget, as {{ settings.<name> }} (it renders as @data/<name>): the chart follows it as it changes.
A demo house to try

A device that is on lights up, and a preset lights up while it is what the device is now. The line under the name says how the device is, like “On · 62%” or “Locked”. Lights, sockets, blinds, sensors and appliances get their own moving icon instead of a plain one. Flows and moods show whether they ran or failed. Buttons that can’t be used, like an unavailable device, are greyed out.
A device to draw, e.g. {{ d.id }}; must be this tile’s own or one its settings chose.
A device whose light it shows, e.g. {{ settings.device.id }}: on, a lamp’s shade lights up in the light’s colour, anything else glows.
A device: a setting’s settings.<name>.id. Left out, the tile’s own device.
A dollhouse to turn and zoom (Pro).

A door in its frame for a contact sensor: it swings open on its hinge (past where it stops, and back) with the light of the room beyond showing through, and swings shut with a small bounce. Its colour is the text colour around it. Reduced motion: no swing; e-ink snaps.

A doorbell with a camera shows its picture between the name and the status, and tapping the picture opens it big. Tiles that are low have no room for the picture and keep the bell. The battery shows in the header when the doorbell has one.

A drawing of your home’s power: solar, the grid, the home battery, the car and the house, with lines between them that light up and move while power flows, quicker the more there is. It finds your parts by itself, and follows the meters you chose under Settings › Energy.
A fan’s speed 0–1, e.g. {{ cap.dim.value }}. Or a live capability of any device, followed and fitted into its own range: {{ cap.measure_battery }} (0–100) just works.
A filter after a | turns a value into what the tile shows: {{ cap.measure_power.value | unit: 'W' }} writes 1.82 kW.
A flow this big is full speed.
A flow to draw as a button; must be one its settings chose.
A frame with a cap, painted in the tile’s background: its bars and the elbow’s inner curves.
A gentle pool, so the plan stays easy to read.
A grain over tiles, or none.
A group of buttons: switch devices, start Flows and Moods, open dashboards.
A handler such as data-hd-on-click runs one or more actions, separated by ;. Up to eight per tap.
A handmade clay diorama.
A heading over a hairline, or a raised card.
A heading.

A heat pump, heater, pump, fan or air conditioner that answers being switched (a fan spins up or winds down, a pump hums, a heater’s flame blooms), then rests. While it works it shows it in colour with a soft glow (warm heating, cool cooling, accent running) and keeps a calm motion going: a fan turns with its speed, a heat pump’s fan turns, a heater’s flame flickers, a pump pulses, an air conditioner breathes. Reduced motion: no motion; e-ink snaps.

A history chart with an hd-series inside per line (up to 8, any devices, also for one line); can sit behind the widget content as a background. Lines with the same unit share an axis, a second unit goes on the right; from two lines on it has a legend, and its tooltip lists every line at that moment.
A key light, a fill and a rim light, for its shape.
A label on the left and a value with its unit on the right, for lists of readings.
A label per bar, separated by commas (Mon,Tue…); some are left out when they don’t fit.
A larger title in the theme’s heading font, like a dashboard heading.
A layout per screen
A level of your house from above, with each room’s temperature.
A light bulb that blooms on and fades off, and spills its light around it, wider and stronger the brighter it is (the tile clips it). Reduced motion fades; e-ink snaps without a glow.
A light or anything that switches on and off. While it is on, a lamp’s shade lights up in the light’s colour and any other model glows; a tap switches it.

A light’s colour on a wheel (hue round the edge, saturation from the white middle out) and its whites on a disk from cool at the top to warm at the bottom; a light with both shows Colour and White above it. Bound to the light’s light_hue (or light_temperature for a light with whites only), it reads the light’s saturation, temperature and mode itself, and sends the colour on release (with `live` also while it is dragged). Below it the account’s favourite colours, up to 15: a tap sets one, + keeps the colour shown, holding one or right-clicking it offers to remove it. On a paired screen or a share link they are shown, not changed. With hue, saturation, temperature and mode and a data-hd-on-change handler, the handler gets { mode: "color", hue, saturation } or { mode: "temperature", temperature }.
A line for each reading, in its own colour, with a figure for each under the chart.
A line that stays flat until the reading changes. Right for readings that jump, like a price or an on and off state.
A line under the title, in the theme’s text font.
A line with the space under it filled in. A calm picture of how a reading moves.
A line you type.
A line, a filled area, columns or steps. The chart’s by default; with several lines only the first is an area.
A line, a filled area, columns, stacked columns, or steps; each hd-series can have its own.
A list as one text, joined with the separator.
A list sorted.
A little bolder.
A little door swings open or shut with the sensor, and the tile says Open (in the warning colour) or Closed. Underneath, it tells you since when it has been open, or when it last changed.

A live flow as a small moving glyph: water drops falling, a gas flame flickering, power pulsing, quicker and fuller as more flows; still and faint at zero. Reduced motion and e-ink: still, with its fullness shown.
A live number that counts to new values (or snaps, on e-ink).

A living background for a tile that heats or cools: soft reds and ambers rising like warm air, or ice blues sinking and drifting. Stronger the harder it works. Position it behind the content; it never takes a tap. Reduced motion: still colour; e-ink: nothing.

A living sky that fills its tile, under the content: the condition’s sky by day or night, toned to the theme, with the sun, stars, drifting clouds, rain, snow, lightning or fog moving in it. Reduced motion: still; e-ink: none.

A lock that locks and unlocks with a springy motion (the shackle drops in and bounces, swings open). While busy the shackle wiggles; when a busy lock ends where it began (refused, or never answered) it shakes.
A map in full colour, with roads, parks and water clearly marked.

A map with a pin for each hd-map-pin inside it; pins glide when they move and the map follows them, framing all or one. Light or dark with the theme. Reduced motion jumps; e-ink is a still map in greys. Lists the places where maps can’t be drawn.
A mark for each hour only.
A mark for every minute (the hours bolder), the twelve hours written out, or only the hours.
A mark for every minute, the hours bolder.
A mood or flow on a room’s card (F22), written inside its hd-room (often in a {% for scene in room.scenes %}); draws nothing itself. The card shows them as buttons in this order.
A mood to draw as a button; must be one its settings chose.
A name over the tiles, such as Radio. Leave it empty for a group without a title.
A name per reading for the legend and the totals, separated by commas.
A name: letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.

A new group starts on a quiet panel, a little lighter than the dashboard on a dark theme and a little darker on a light one. Style… gives it any background a tile can have: a colour, a gradient or one of your pictures, with its corners, border and shadow. The tiles inside keep their own look.
A number as text with exactly n decimals (0–3), with the region's decimal mark: 21 | decimals: 1 → "21.0" ("21,0" in the Netherlands); — when empty.
A number rounded, to 0 decimals unless given: 21.456 | round: 1 → 21.5.
A pale map, whatever the theme.

A part of the widget that folds open and closed under a heading, like the sections of the widget settings; while closed it shows `summary`. To remember it per screen, bind `open` to the widget’s state and keep each change: `open="{{ state.schedule }}" data-hd-on-change="setState('schedule', event.value)"`. Without that it still folds, but starts over when the widget is drawn anew.

A paused speaker keeps its last track, dimmed. Smaller tiles show less: a square tile drops the artwork, the volume and the progress, and a small one keeps the name and one big play button. Wide tiles put the artwork beside the controls, tall ones above them.

A period as bars against the previous one: each value a bar in its colour with a soft glow, the previous period’s value behind it as an outline, the running bar (`current`) drawn as “so far”, values below zero hanging under the line. Hover or tap a bar to read both. Bars grow in at full motion only; flat on e-ink. For any series of numbers: an hour by hour day, a week, a month.

A picture of a house with your home’s power pointed out on it: solar on the roof, the grid’s box at the edge of the garden, what the house uses, the home battery and the car in the garage. Its parts follow your energy meters, like the Energy flow, and on Tiledash’s pictures the solar panels, the car and the battery only show when your home has them.
A picture of this level made in the floor planner. Without one, the tile shows the live plan.

A picture on the web: an https: or http: address; anything else is ignored. A widget with a script, and a Community widget from 19 December 2026, shows it only from a host its manifest names in `images` (`script.images` with a script), or when the user typed the address in a setting.
A picture the user uploaded, by its id (the custom tile’s pictures). Shown only to its owner; the page fetches it and hands over an address, so the widget never sees a link.

A picture: a web address (`src`, http or https only), one of the device’s own images by name (`image`, e.g. album art as `albumart`, a camera’s `snapshot`) a picture the user uploaded (`upload`, its id) or a person’s (`person`, their id: `settings.who.id`, `people[0].id`). It is fetched without referrer or cookies, loads lazily, fades in, and shows the `fallback` icon while it loads, when there is none and when it fails; grey on e-ink. It fills its parent, so size the element (or its parent) in CSS.
A piece of furniture or your own 3D model, in 2.5D or turned any way in 3D.
A play/pause button face that turns from one into the other; it shows what a tap does. Reduced motion: a fade; e-ink snaps.
A plug and socket that snap together when it switches on and pull apart when it switches off, with a short pulse from the joint when power starts to flow. Reduced motion fades; e-ink snaps.
A progress ring for a fraction (battery, solar share, cover position).
A quarter turn clockwise.
A quarter turn the other way.
A question to ask first, e.g. “Run Leaving home?”.
A quick change, like a press. 0ms when nothing may move.

A ranking of the devices that used the most electricity today, biggest first. Each has a bar against the biggest, its share of the electricity taken from the grid today and roughly what it cost. Under the list, what the rest used. Tap a device to open its details.

A reading’s history as a grid, a row per day and a column per hour, each cell coloured from --hd-heatmap-low to --hd-heatmap-high (the accent) by its value; hovering a cell names its time and value. Reads the history again every ten minutes and says so when the reading isn’t recorded. Parts: ::part(cell), ::part(axis).
A room to focus on, e.g. {{ settings.plan.room.id }}; empty for the whole level.
A round clock face with hands.
A row of dots, one for each page. Swipe sideways, or tap a dot, to turn the page. Good for a few pages that need no names.
A row of tabs, one for each page, that you tap. The tabs show the page’s name, its icon or both, set under Tabs show.
A row per day, or the range folded into a typical week (a row per weekday, each hour the average).
A second value shown as a dot on the dial, e.g. the current temperature. Or a live capability of any device, followed: {{ settings.x.cap.measure_power }}.
A second value shown as a dot, e.g. the room temperature. Or a live capability of any device, followed: {{ settings.x.cap.measure_power }}.
A second value shown as a line across the bar, e.g. a target. Or a live capability of any device, followed: {{ settings.x.cap.measure_power }}.

A sectional door rolls up and down with the real one, its light blinking while it moves. The tile says Closed in green or Open in amber, with how long ago that changed, and one button: Open when closed, Close when open.

A sensor or alarm that says it went off, with its own icon: motion pings like a radar (then calmly while it still sees movement), smoke, CO and the siren shake and pulse while on, water ripples under a bobbing drop, a doorbell swings and rings twice. Its colour is the text colour around it. Reduced motion: a still halo; e-ink snaps.
A short line beside the heading while closed, e.g. “Next: 21° at 17:00”.

A slider bound to a numeric capability (dim, target temperature, volume…) with bind (or the explicit form: value with data-hd-on-change). It sends the value once, on release. With `fill` it is the whole tile: put it in the tile and the template’s own content inside it (`<hd-slider fill bind="…">name and value</hd-slider>`); its value is a wash rising from the bottom (or growing from the left) with a grip on its edge, dragged anywhere by how far it moves; a tap glides it to the tapped spot, or with `tap="tile"` is the tile’s own tap. A fill slider’s colours are CSS properties, any colour or gradient: `--hd-slider-tone` (the edge and grip), `--hd-slider-fill` (the wash, laid across the whole tile and uncovered as it grows) and `--hd-slider-track` (the rest).
A slider’s track thickness.
A slow change, like a theme switching.
A small heading.

A small history line with live updates, an hd-series inside per line (up to 3, any devices, also for one line); no axes, legend or tooltip, so label the lines around it. Lines with the same unit share a scale.
A small line of capitals in a quiet colour, so the tiles stay what you look at. The default.

A small window shows the cover at its position: blinds roll up and down, curtains bunch to the sides, and the slats move while the motor runs. Beside it, the tile says Open, Closed or a percentage, and Opening or Closing while it moves.
A smaller chart below the figures, so you can read it properly.
A soft card behind each item, so it stands out as an item.
A soft version of the lit colour, for washes and glows.
A solid rounded bar with the chosen tab filled in the accent colour. The same tabs other widgets use.
A springy easing, for things that bounce into place.
A state name.

A still, faded map behind a tile’s content (A.1), centred on a place, with the hd-map-pin children as small marks; the place moves over the picture and a new picture is drawn once it leaves the middle. A picture, not a live map: no WebGL per tile. E-ink: grey. Reduced motion: no fades or gliding.

A straight bar filled up to a value within a range: progress, a level, how full a tank or bin is. Sideways, or filling from the bottom up with orientation="vertical". It draws only the bar; write the value next to it. Its thickness is the CSS variable --hd-meter-size (10px sideways; the full width upright), its rounding --hd-meter-round. Parts: ::part(bar), ::part(fill).

A strip under the dial says what the device is doing: heating, hot water, standby or a fault for a boiler that reports it, with water temperatures and the pressure (amber below 1 bar, red below 0.8); the status and a countdown for a cooker; heating or ready for a water heater. A plain thermostat shows none. On a tile two rows high there is no room for the dial, so you get the numbers with minus and plus buttons.

A theme colour name (accent, lit, cool, good, warn, danger, text, surface, canvas, chart-1…chart-6) or #rrggbb: whatever a Colour setting gives.
A theme colour name or #rrggbb for one reading or a total; lines get the theme’s chart colours.
A theme colour name or #rrggbb for the node it comes from.
A theme colour name or #rrggbb; the theme’s chart colours in order by default (repeats are dashed).

A washer, dryer or dishwasher counts as busy while it draws power, a charger while it charges, a speaker while it plays. For anything else you say what makes it busy. New items fade in. Behind it all there can be a living sky: sun, stars, clouds, rain, snow or fog, matching the weather out there and the time of day. The forecast comes from MET Norway and is credited on the tile. Offline, it keeps the last forecast and says how old it is.
